Published online:
September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States (global FX market context)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
A Reuters poll of FX strategists finds the dollar likely to hold firm near-term but weaken in a year. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's sparse and ambiguous guidance leaves markets uncertain on rate trajectory. Rate futures price in two hikes this year, but most strategists and economists (notably BNY's Reinhart) believe the Fed will tighten less than priced. The 10-year Treasury hit ~4.82%, U.S. debt topped $40T, and net long dollar positions are declining. Geopolitical risk (U.S.-Iran conflict) adds upside dollar uncertainty. Strategists are marginally skewed toward dollar weakness over the next three months.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (The article centers on Fed rate path uncertainty, 10-year Treasury yields, dollar direction, and their interplay — all core US macro/rates topics)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 60 (Markets are pricing two Fed hikes this year, and Warsh's hawkish remarks are noted, making rate increases a live scenario being actively discussed)
Probability of increase: 45%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 30 (Some strategists implicitly lean toward less tightening than priced, suggesting rates could hold, but this is not the dominant framing)
Probability of holding: 25%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (Reinhart suggests the Fed won't tighten as much as priced, but outright cuts are not explicitly discussed)
Probability of decrease: 15%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +25 (Lean hawkish — Warsh's hawkish remarks, two hikes priced in by futures, and a near-3-year high 10Y yield of 4.82% tilt the tone modestly hawkish, but broad strategist skepticism that the Fed will follow through tempers this significantly)
